data.name: Corona Blossom Vol.3 Journey to the Stars
data.detailed_description:
"Corona Blossom" is a heartwarming trilogy of visual novels featuring the "e-mote" system and artwork by nanaca mai!

Learn the fates of the characters you've grown to know and love in the exciting final chapter of the Corona Blossom saga!

STORY:
R-ne: a cute, shapeshifting metallic lifeform who one day fell from space.
Keiji Osaki: a young man with a mysterious past, now working at a mech garage.

After growing close through adventures and mishaps throughout the summer, the two of them made a promise: to return R-ne to her home planet.

To that end, Keiji has steadily been working on a plan together with space pirate Lily, and his coworker at the garage, Kumiko.

But Ms. Kanade's big reveal has thrown a spanner in the works.

The people of Hanma Town must now do battle against a mysterious organization that's after R-ne.
Time is running out for Keiji and his friends!

Will they ever be able to return R-ne to space?
And is that really the right move?

The thrilling conclusion to R-ne's journey is finally here!

reviews.review:
Here we are. We have gotten to Corona Blossom Vol. 3 Journey to the Stars, the thrilling and heartwarming conclusion to this trilogy. After the ending of the last volume, I was excited to see how things would go here. Will Keiji and his friends successfully send R-ne to space? Let's see. 

Good to see that the writers are still consistent with how they mix serious and comedic moments into the plot. The shift in tone is not too sudden for things to feel like something was missing. Another commendable thing is how the first couple of parts are very serious. Those moments successfully keep you tense for the entire duration. Thankfully, the story does not lose its steam once it returns to the usual tone you would expect from this trilogy. For the most part, it is a very fascinating story with many good moments for the characters as well as a few thought-provoking conversations. And the ending? Very satisfying and provides you with some good visuals to boot. I never get tired of a VN using its OP as BGM during a memorable scene. 

So that is all, right? Corona Blossom has a consistent story with nice visuals and music that gives you a sweet ending. While none of the characters are too memorable, almost all of them are likable and nicely written. It even made good use of background characters. What is not to like? Well...

[h3]What went wrong?[/h3]
[olist]
[*] [b]Kanade.[/b] I thought everything that was done with her in the last volume was effective. Then, volume 3 threw in too much that was tough to follow in the same story with a metal blob alien. Apparently, Kanade [spoiler]has two people in her body: herself and an angel. Beltiel, the angel, is the evil one who wants to advance the human race by any means necessary.[/spoiler] Bringing [spoiler]angels[/spoiler] out of nowhere was a weird choice, but then they decided to also reveal that [spoiler]Kanade is really an alien who lost her memories years ago.[/spoiler] Revealing all of this in the last part of the trilogy when nothing in the previous volumes hinted at any of this was certainly a choice.
[*][b]Linear storytelling.[/b] [url=https://vndb.org/w13248]This review[/url] stayed in my head while I was reading volumes 2 and 3. It is hard not to agree with many of the points said after finishing the trilogy. Corona Blossom's story only having one path means other plot points either lack the necessary time in the story or are forgotten. For example, one scene in the first two volumes shows the reader that [spoiler]Kumiko has a thing for Keiji.[/spoiler] Unfortunately, the story forgets about this plot point in the last volume because it has other ideas. It constantly makes me wonder what could have been. 
[*][b]Unresolved plot points and unanswered questions.[/b] This is a continuation of the last point. I did enjoy the ending, but it was not until I thought about it more that I realized how many things were left unresolved. [spoiler]Lily and Yunie are stuck on Earth with no way of getting back into space & Lala's whereabouts still being unknown[/spoiler] are a few of the unresolved plot points that I just have to accept. As for the answered questions, I could ramble about the existence of [spoiler]angels,[/spoiler] but there is something else that needs to be addressed. After everything, how could the story not tell us [spoiler]what happened to Keiji's parents?[/spoiler] I do not understand how the writers missed that. 
[*][b]The lip sync issues[/b] are a small problem that I feel I should talk about. Volume 3 is the one in the trilogy where the character mouth animations mess up the most. I have no idea why.
[/olist]

[h3]Final thoughts on Corona Blossom Volume 3 & the entire trilogy[/h3]
Despite my feelings about volume 3, I cannot deny that I did enjoy most of my time with this VN. Sadly, everything crumbled after I finished it and realized how much untapped potential there was. Overall, the Corona Blossom trilogy is decent. It starts strong in its first volume before slowly dipping in quality. The decision to give this VN a linear story results in too much plot, resulting in many things being left unanswered or underutilized. If you are looking for a mostly lighthearted story with comedy you would find in harem and fanservice-heavy anime, then I can recommend Corona Blossom to you. Its characters, music, and visuals are great. Additionally, despite my feelings about the ending, the story is enjoyable if you just focus on the main plot point (sending R-ne to space). 

Who knows? You might enjoy it a lot more than I did.
